children: management said that as a result of 35K fewer trucks delivered during the next generation pickup changeover, the fourth quarter of 2026 is expected to be "seasonally weaker" than the second and third quarters of this year.

Speaking at the Morgan Stanley 14th Annual Laguna Conference, chief financial officer Paul Jacobson remarked that if things don’t get out of balance, “Fourth quarter is typically seasonally weaker than Q2 and Q3 this year…seasonally less than 35K units is about the right way to think about Q4."
Jacobson also noted that 2027 is “going to be a bit of a flat spot” for EVs.

“EV profitability has been hit really hard over the last couple of years. First, tariffs; second, everybody was logging EV credits as part of the variable profit equation…both of those went the wrong direction against profitability.”
The company still believes EVs are a long-term play, “but we’ve got to get them profitable,” something Jacobson believes GM is outperforming its rivals on.

title: General Motors' CFO expects Q4 to be seasonally weaker
